subject: Acme Health - org bootstrapping and API access setup
messages:
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Nadia Brooks <nadia.brooks@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:15:00 -0400
Subject: Initial rollout - org structure and keys

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the intro last week. We're ready to start the first-phase rollout for our integration with Redwood. Before our kickoff, can you confirm how you recommend we structure organizations/projects for production vs staging, and what the best practice is for API key provisioning and rotation? Our compliance team prefers a strict separation between environments and wants all keys centrally auditable.

A couple specifics:
- We'll have a single engineering org, but want separate projects for dev/staging/prod.
- We need short-lived API keys where possible, and role-based access so only ops can create keys.

Can your team share a checklist so we can map these requirements to your platform?

Thanks,
Sam
Senior Platform Engineer
Acme Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial rollout - org structure and keys

Hi Sam — great to hear the team is ready. I'm looping in Dev (solutions engineer) and Lauren (onboarding lead) so we can provide an actionable plan and the docs you asked for.

Quick answers up front: we typically recommend one Redwood tenant per company, with separate "projects" for dev/staging/prod inside the tenant. Each project gets isolated resource and billing views, and you can pin models/variants per project to enforce parity.

For API keys and rotation:
- Use short-lived API keys backed by our token service where possible (12h-30d).
- Operational roles (Ops, Infra Admin) are the only roles we recommend for key creation.
- We support centralized audit logs and KMS-integrated key wrapping for production keys.

Next steps: Dev will propose a minimal onboarding checklist and role matrix; Lauren will prepare invites and the initial project scaffolding. Can we target tomorrow (Mon 2026-05-04) for a 30-min technical handoff? If that works, please confirm availability.

Cheers,
Monica
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial rollout - org structure and keys

Hi Sam — quick tech checklist to align with compliance and make the handoff smooth: 

1) Tenant and projects
- Recommendation: 1 tenant: "acme-health". Projects: "acme-dev", "acme-staging", "acme-prod".
- Each project should have dedicated model pinning and quota limits.

2) Identity & access
- Create the following roles in order of privileges: Viewer, Developer, Ops, Admin.
- Only Admin + Ops can mint long-lived keys; Developer role gets short-lived tokens for CI (via service-account flow).

3) Keys & rotation
- Use service accounts for CI/CD: short-lived tokens (recommended 8-24 hours) minted by our token service.
- For integrations that must use long-lived keys, store wrapped keys in your KMS and record key_id in Redwood project metadata.

4) Audit & compliance
- Enable per-project audit logs (we stream to customer-owned S3 or CloudWatch).
- We can forward token-issue events and key-rotation records to your SIEM.

5) Environment separation
- Enforce model access control lists so staging cannot call prod-backed models.
- Consider separate billing accounts for prod to simplify chargebacks.

Attachments: onboarding checklist (Monica and Lauren will attach the official PDF and IAM CSV).

I can run the 30-min tech handoff and walk through a live demo of creating a service account and minting a token. Proposed slots: Mon 4 May 14:00 or 16:00 ET.

- Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- For the CI short-lived tokens, we plan to use GitHub Actions; will the service-account flow integrate with GH OIDC?

We can do 16:00 ET today for the handoff; that time works for Nadia and me. Sending calendar invite now.

Hi all — attaching our onboarding artifacts and the initial IAM matrix for your review. See attachments: redwood_onboarding_checklist.pdf (step-by-step) and acme_iam_matrix.csv (role -> permissions mapping).

Quick notes from Ops perspective: 
- We will provision the tenant and scaffold three projects in a staging mode first; you will receive invites for two Admin users and one Ops service account.
- For S3 log forwarding: we forward events to a customer-owned bucket via a secure transfer role; retention is controlled by the customer's lifecycle policy on the bucket. We keep a short-lived copy for troubleshooting (30 days) unless you ask us to retain longer under an enterprise agreement.
- GitHub Actions OIDC: yes, we support OIDC provider integrations for service accounts to mint short-lived tokens. We'll include a sample workflow in the Drive link.
